in_os_smoke.method: Not attempted in-lane: requires the full desktop boot (disk.img with DESKTOP/BROWSER/ICU/sqlite) + QMP keystrokes (run_console_test.py drives the WORKSTATION tree, which is off-limits), OR a kernel mode hook to boot MCOPY directly -- and acceptance.md 5.2 assigns MODE=selfhost + SELFHOST.BIN to the wave-2 HARNESS lane / parent (kernel change).
in_os_smoke.deferred_reason: No AUTORUN mechanism in the shell today (acceptance.md 5.2); the primary in-OS driver (MODE=selfhost launching SELFHOST.BIN) is a kernel change owned by the harness lane; the QMP keystroke fallback needs the full desktop+console boot which is heavy and explicitly the weaker path. A lane-local kernel edit is out of scope (single-writer rule: kernel changes are parent-owned).
wave3_steps: 1. make disk.img (full OS incl. the new ::/TOOLS/MCOPY.BIN|MDEL.BIN|MMD.BIN staged by this lane's Makefile block)
2. Boot per acceptance.md 5.1 (qemu-system-aarch64, EDK2, -serial file:SERIAL.log, virtio-blk + the 8-core/16GB line)

3. Primary driver (harness lane): MODE=selfhost -> SELFHOST.BIN runs `mcopy -i /SRC/OUT.IMG <payload> ::</SRC/...` and mmd ::/BOOT ::/TOOLS ::/SRC; assert [SELFHOST] phase=s3-disk-done + zero FAIL tokens

4. Fallback keystrokes (if SELFHOST.BIN not ready): boot desktop, open the console (CONSOLE.BIN via Apps menu), type 'MMD -i /TMP/X.IMG ::/TOOLS' then 'MCOPY -i /TMP/X.IMG <file> ::/TOOLS/FILE.TXT' and 'MDEL -i /TMP/X.IMG ::/TOOLS/FILE.TXT', then verify via file extraction (fat16img.py get) that the copy-in round-trip matches (LFN names exercise vfat.c)
5. Evacuate the scratch image / copy-back for byte-compare; verdict = marker substring + zero FAIL/FAILED tokens (acceptance 8.4)

mcopy -s (local-directory recursion) needs working opendir/readdir, which is ENOSYS in the sysroot today (audit 4.2). Ported code compiles the non-recurse path on target; -s verified on host where glibc readdir exists. Acceptance recipes use individual-file MCOPY lines (no -s), so no acceptance blocker.
notes: Upstream builds one multicall 'mtools' binary dispatching on argv[0]; HobbyOS loads one flat .BIN per program, so the port links each command separately: shared engine objects (mtools_*) + one tiny main per tool (mtoolsm_* from mtools_port.c, -DMTOOLS_TOOL_*). mtools.c/expand.c/precmd.c not transcribed - the port glue replaces them (expand/$(...) shell expansion and post-commands are unreachable for -i IMG; documented deviation). HobbyOS glue in config.h is gated by HOBBYOS_TARGET; HOST_TEST retargets HAVE_TZSET/STRNDUP/READDIR for the parity harness.
